newsitem.title: USA: U.S. carrier's captain tells crew "Be prepared...".
newsitem.headline: U.S. carrier's captain tells crew "Be prepared...".

text.p: "Be prepared for what lies ahead...Be prepared for further tasking," U.S. Navy Captain Larry Baucom told his aircraft carrier crew on Tuesday after fighter pilots returned from escort duty with B-52 bombers over Iraq.
Speaking over the carrier's loudspeaker system, the commanding officer told the 5,000 people aboard: "I thank those who woke up so early to make breakfast for the pilots."

"We exercise command and control for the launching of this strike," Rear Admiral Edward Moore told reporters on board the carrier in the northern Gulf. "The planes from the Carl Vinson provided air patrol to the B-52s."
The B-52 bombers and two warships early on Tuesday fired 27 cruise missiles at military sites in southern Iraq to punish Baghdad for an assault against Kurds in the north.
"The strikes were ordered as a warning to Iraq to adhere to requirements outlined in United Nations resolutions," Moore told reporters.

Giving details of what he called Operation Desert Strike, Moore said 13 missiles were fired from two B-52 bombers flying from Guam in the Pacific and 14 were fired from the USS Laboon guided missile destroyer and the USS Shilo cruiser in the Gulf.
"At 7:15 this morning (0415 GMT) U.S. naval and air forces executed air strikes against Iraqi military sites," he said.

"The strikes were conducted with both shipboard-launched Tomahawk cruise missiles and conventional air-launched cruise missiles and were directed against Iraqi air defence sites and command and control facilities," Moore said.
Asked whether he knew of any Iraqi retaliation, Moore said: "I don't know of any firing or any response by Iraq."

"We are always in a state of readiness to respond to any contingencies that might come up," the admiral said. "I don't want to go beyond what kind of state of readiness it is but we are always prepared to respond to any contingency."
Moore, answering questions, said he felt U.S. forces in the Gulf were not in particular danger. "The strike for this morning has been completed," he said.

Earlier, F-14D pilot Lieutenant Eric Atshuler from San Diego, California told reporters: "I am here to support and defend the U.S. constitution, so any orders that the nation's command has, I'm here to carry them out.
"With Carl Vinson and airwing 14 (20 F-14Ds) you've got the best the navy has to offer."
"The toughest thing to me in the Gulf is the heat," said Lieutenant Mike Steffen, a helicopter pilot from Bedford, Virginia. "I don't want to go to war as much as anybody else."

Officers said the Carl Vinson battlegroup in the Gulf comprised the carrier itself, one supply ship, three cruisers, one frigate and one submarine. They declined to say how many other U.S. warships were in the strategic waterway.
